In [[mathematics]] &mdash; specifically, in [[stochastic analysis]] &mdash; the '''Green measure''' is a [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] associated to an [[Itō diffusion]].  There is an associated '''Green formula''' representing suitably [[smooth function]]s in terms of the Green measure and [[first exit time]]s of the diffusion.  The concepts are named after the [[United Kingdom|British]] [[mathematician]] [[George Green (mathematician)|George Green]] and are generalizations of the classical [[Green's function]] and Green formula to the stochastic case using [[Dynkin's formula]].

==Notation==

Let ''X'' be an '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>-valued Itō diffusion satisfying an Itō [[stochastic differential equation]] of the form

:<math>\mathrm{d} X_{t} = b(X_{t}) \, \mathrm{d} t + \sigma (X_{t}) \, \mathrm{d} B_{t}.</math>

Let '''P'''<sup>''x''</sup> denote the [[probability measure|law]] of ''X'' given the initial condition ''X''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''x'', and let '''E'''<sup>''x''</sup> denote [[expected value|expectation]] with respect to '''P'''<sup>''x''</sup>. Let ''L''<sub>''X''</sub> be the [[Infinitesimal generator (stochastic processes)|infinitesimal generator]] of ''X'', i.e.

:<math>L_{X} = \sum_{i} b_{i} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_{i}} + \frac1{2} \sum_{i, j} \big( \sigma \sigma^{\top} \big)_{i, j} \frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial x_{i} \, \partial x_{j}}.</math>

Let ''D''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> be an [[open set|open]], [[bounded set|bounded]] domain; let ''&tau;''<sub>''D''</sub> be the [[first exit time]] of ''X'' from ''D'':

:<math>\tau_{D} := \inf \{ t \geq 0 | X_{t} \not \in D \}.</math>

==The Green measure==

Intuitively, the Green measure of a Borel set ''H'' (with respect to a point ''x'' and domain ''D'') is the expected length of time that ''X'', having started at ''x'', stays in ''H'' before it leaves the domain ''D''.  That is, the '''Green measure''' of ''X'' with respect to ''D'' at ''x'', denoted ''G''(''x'',&nbsp;⋅), is defined for Borel sets ''H''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> by

:<math>G(x, H) = \mathbf{E}^{x} \left[ \int_{0}^{\tau_{D}} \chi_{H} (X_{s}) \, \mathrm{d} s \right],</math>

or for bounded, continuous functions ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''D''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' by

:<math>\int_{D} f(y) \, G(x, \mathrm{d} y) = \mathbf{E}^{x} \left[ \int_{0}^{\tau_{D}} f(X_{s}) \, \mathrm{d} s \right]</math>

The name "Green measure" comes from the fact that if ''X'' is [[Brownian motion]], then

:<math>G(x, H) = \int_{H} G(x, y) \, \mathrm{d} y,</math>

where ''G''(''x'',&nbsp;''y'') is Green's function for the operator ''L''<sub>''X''</sub> (which, in the case of Brownian motion, is {{sfrac|1|2}}Δ, where Δ is the [[Laplace operator]]) on the domain ''D''.

==The Green formula==

Suppose that '''E'''<sup>''x''</sup>[''&tau;''<sub>''D''</sub>]&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;+&infin; for all ''x''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;''D'', and let ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' be of [[smooth function|smoothness class ''C''<sup>2</sup>]] with [[compact support]]. Then

:<math>f(x) = \mathbf{E}^{x} \big[ f \big( X_{\tau_{D}} \big) \big] - \int_{D} L_{X} f (y) \, G(x, \mathrm{d} y).</math>

In particular, for ''C''<sup>2</sup> functions ''f'' with support [[compactly embedded]] in ''D'',

:<math>f(x) = - \int_{D} L_{X} f (y) \, G(x, \mathrm{d} y).</math>

The proof of Green's formula is an easy application of Dynkin's formula and the definition of the Green measure:

:<math>\mathbf{E}^{x} \big[ f \big( X_{\tau_{D}} \big) \big]</math>
::<math>= f(x) + \mathbf{E}^{x} \left[ \int_{0}^{\tau_{D}} L_{X} f (X_{s}) \, \mathrm{d} s \right]</math>
::<math>= f(x) + \int_{D} L_{X} f (y) \, G(x, \mathrm{d} y).</math>
